raw_case_text:
A 48-year-old woman was brought to our emergency department because of confusion and incoherent speech. A striking abdominal distention was noted. The patient was not known to have any underlying medical or psychological illnesses and previously had not had any symptoms or complaints. On physical examination, she was alert but disoriented, with no focal neurological deficit. Results of the cardiopulmonary examination were normal. Shifting dullness was elicited on abdominal examination, but the abdomen was soft and nontender. Results of the initial laboratory parameters revealed anemia with hemoglobin of 8.4 g/dL (normocytic/normochromic anemia), white blood cell count 10.3 x 103/muL with left shift, and platelet count 181 x 103/muL. She had renal dysfunction with a serum creatinine level of 3.5 mg/dL. Liver chemistry revealed an albumin level of 2 g/dL, total protein 8.8 g/dL, total bilirubin 1.7 mg/dL, and aspartate aminotransferase 71 IU/mL; otherwise, she had normal liver enzymes. The ammonia level was 28 mol/L. The patient was positive for HIV-1 RNA, but <20 copies/mL were detected, with a CD4 count of 335 cells/mm3, and she had negative viral hepatitis markers. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging of the head showed multiple, bilateral, acute lacunar infarcts with a distribution suggesting an embolic origin. The echocardiography showed no abnormalities, and normal results from the cerebrospinal fluid examination ruled out acute bacterial meningitis. To investigate the abdominal distension, computed tomography and ultrasound imaging of the abdomen were performed, which showed hepatomegaly with mild surface nodularity, massive ascites, and normal spleen size. Abdominal paracentesis was performed, and the fluid analysis results were as follows: white blood cell count 443 cells/mm3, absolute neutrophil count 389 cells/mm3, lactic dehydrogenase 221 IU/L, glucose 72 mg/dL, amylase 45 IU/L, albumin 1.7 g/dL, serum ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) 0.1, protein 6.8 g/dL, and adenosine deaminase activity level 15.8 IU/L (normal = 7.6). Ascitic bacterial and mycobacterial cultures were negative.
Because of the anemia, kidney failure, and albumin protein dissociation, serum protein electrophoresis was performed, which showed an M spike in the beta1-globulin region (see Table 1 for detailed analysis). Serum immunoglobulin levels were as follows: IgM 20 mg/dL, IgG 4.3 mg/dL, IgE 27 kU/L, and IgA 6,033 mg/dL. Protein electrophoresis of the ascitic fluid showed an M spike in the beta-globulin region (Fig. 1). Serum, urine and peritoneal fluid immunofixation showed IgA lambda monoclonal proteins, which confirmed peritoneal infiltration of myelomatous cells. Bone marrow biopsy presented diffuse infiltration by well-differentiated plasma cells, which comprised 49-52% of the nucleated hematopoietic cells. Results of flow cytometry showed lambda light chain restriction consistent with MM. The serum beta2-microglobulin level was 12.5 mg/L, and the skeletal survey was negative, indicating stage III MM according to both the Durie-Salmon staging system and the International Staging System. The patient was discharged to a nursing home and planned to receive follow-up care in the hematology clinic to begin treatment with bortezomib and dexamethasone.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 48-year-old female presenting with acute confusion, incoherent speech, and marked abdominal distension.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was brought to the emergency department after family noted acute confusion and incoherent speech. She had no previous medical complaints or known chronic conditions. Concurrently, striking abdominal enlargement was noted, prompting admission for neurological and gastrointestinal evaluation.
subjective.past_medical_history: No known underlying medical, psychological, or chronic illnesses.
subjective.review_of_systems: Acute confusion, incoherent speech, abdominal distension; denies prior fever, headache, focal motor deficits, dyspnea, chest pain, or gastrointestinal bleeding.

objective.physical_examination: General: Alert but disoriented to time and place; no focal cranial nerve or motor deficits. Cardiopulmonary: Normal heart sounds, clear lungs. Abdomen: Striking abdominal distension with positive shifting dullness on percussion; abdomen soft, non-tender, without guarding.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: Hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL (normocytic, normochromic anemia), white blood cell count 10.3 x 10^3/microL with left shift, platelet count 181 x 10^3/microL. Renal & Metabolic: Serum creatinine 3.5 mg/dL, blood ammonia 28 micromol/L. Liver function: Serum albumin 2.0 g/dL, total protein 8.8 g/dL (albumin-globulin dissociation), total bilirubin 1.7 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 71 IU/mL, with otherwise normal liver enzymes. Viral serology: Acute viral hepatitis markers negative. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis: Normal cell counts, protein, and glucose; bacterial cultures negative. Ascitic fluid analysis: White blood cell count 443 cells/mm3 (absolute neutrophil count 389 cells/mm3), glucose 72 mg/dL, amylase 45 IU/L, lactic dehydrogenase 221 IU/L, albumin 1.7 g/dL, total protein 6.8 g/dL, serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) 0.1, adenosine deaminase (ADA) 15.8 IU/L; bacterial and mycobacterial cultures negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT and MRI: Multiple bilateral acute lacunar infarcts with distribution suggesting an embolic source. Transthoracic echocardiogram: Normal without intracardiac thrombus or vegetations. Abdominal ultrasound and CT: Hepatomegaly with mild surface nodularity, massive ascites, and normal spleen size. Electrophoresis & Immunofixation: Serum protein electrophoresis showed an M-spike in the beta-1 globulin region; ascitic fluid protein electrophoresis showed an M-spike in the beta-globulin region; serum, urine, and peritoneal fluid immunofixation all confirmed IgA lambda monoclonal proteins. Quantitative immunoglobulins: IgA 6,033 mg/dL, IgM 20 mg/dL, IgG 4.3 mg/dL, IgE 27 kU/L; serum beta-2 microglobulin 12.5 mg/L. Bone marrow biopsy: Diffuse marrow infiltration by well-differentiated plasma cells comprising 49-52% of nucleated hematopoietic cells; flow cytometry confirmed lambda light chain restriction. Skeletal survey: Negative for focal lytic lesions.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Multiple myeloma (IgA lambda, Stage III by Durie-Salmon and International Staging System) with myelomatous peritoneal infiltration causing massive ascites, severe acute renal failure, normocytic anemia, and acute embolic lacunar cerebral infarctions, in a patient with asymptomatic human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1) infection (viral load < 20 copies/mL, CD4 count 335 cells/mm3).
Plan & Outcome: Discharged to a skilled nursing facility with plans for outpatient hematology follow-up to commence induction chemotherapy with bortezomib and dexamethasone alongside antiretroviral and supportive care.
